entries.title: Robotics
entries.final_prompt:
Create a premium collectible hobby illustration. The artwork should feel cinematic, aspirational, emotionally warm, commercially polished, and immediately readable on a small mobile card. Use a strong focal subject, crisp subject separation, rich but controlled colour, atmospheric depth, premium lighting, and clear visual storytelling. Sell the emotional fantasy of doing the hobby rather than merely depicting an object. Aim for the feel of a miniature lifestyle hero illustration inside one coherent collectible-art universe, not a poster, advertisement, editorial cover, card face, or designed page. Keep edges and subject readability cleaner than soft editorial painting. No text, no logo, no typography, no card border, no rarity badge, no watermark, no UI.

The hobby or interest name is semantic context only and must never appear visually. Never render the hobby name, title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, body copy, text box, lower-third, or typography-like decoration. Do not reserve blank layout space for text and do not turn the composition into a poster, advertisement, magazine cover, card face, or editorial page. Any incidental real-world surface that could carry writing must be blank, abstract, cropped away, turned away, or too indistinct to read.

Treat every monitor, laptop, tablet, phone, camera display, dashboard, terminal, and digital panel as a physical prop rather than a semantic canvas. Prefer no visible screen surface at all. Recognition must come from the person, physical tool, device, prototype, controller, camera, microphone, hardware, object, or real-world action. If a screen is genuinely unavoidable, show only its back, edge, steep oblique angle, dark/blank surface, or a heavily defocused field of broad colour/image shapes; keep it small and secondary. Never present a front-facing readable display, interface, editing timeline, waveform panel, code window, terminal, menu, chat, dashboard, spreadsheet, labels, controls, icons, or text-like UI structure.

Use this overall composition approach: Show a person physically testing or adjusting a real prototype in an open test area. The prototype, hands, mechanical parts, movement, sensors, wheels, joints, tools, cones, or physical controller carry the idea. The scene contains zero monitors, zero laptops, zero tablets, zero phones, zero televisions, zero computer desks, and zero visible display surfaces. Human-height or slightly low medium-wide field-test framing centered on the prototype and hands, with no office/workstation composition. The emotional feeling should be hands-on discovery, testing, engineering, motion. Make the hobby immediately recognizable through A real physical prototype plus active hands-on testing, adjustment, movement, sensors, mechanical parts, or a physical controller; never a computer screen..

Compose the specific scene this way: An engineer crouches beside a wheeled or articulated generic robot on an open indoor test floor, physically adjusting a joint or sensor while a second person may hold a simple screenless physical remote controller. Use cones, floor markers, mechanical parts, and robot movement as the only context. No desk or computer equipment appears. Low three-quarter medium-wide test-floor view keeping the robot body, hands, wheels/joints/sensors, and open surrounding floor clear. Use Bright neutral test-space light with crisp mechanical detail and painterly cinematic depth..

Use this colour and material direction: cool modern base with controlled warm human accents. avoid generic cyberpunk, show purposeful interaction.

Depict this activity: An engineer physically tests and adjusts one generic wheeled or articulated robot on an open indoor test floor, touching a joint or sensor while the robot moves through simple cones or floor markers

Place it in this believable setting: A bright open robotics test floor with mechanical parts, cones, floor tape, robot wheels, joints and sensors, plus optionally one simple screenless handheld remote controller; no desk, monitor, laptop, tablet, phone, television, desktop computer, terminal, code display, or digital panel anywhere

The emotional tone should feel curiosity, creation, problem-solving, future-facing energy.

Use this activity-specific composition: Make the robot body, engineer's hands, joints, wheels, sensors, and physical test movement fill the storytelling area. The scene contains zero objects with a display surface.

Use this activity-specific camera treatment: Low three-quarter medium-wide field-test view with open floor behind the robot; avoid all desk and workstation framing.

Keep these hobby-recognition cues visible: human actively using Robotics, subfield-specific hardware, output, or process, purposeful interaction, generic robot body with wheels or articulated joints, hands-on adjustment of a physical sensor or joint, open physical test course with cones or floor markers.

The scene must include: a concrete Robotics interaction, one real physical generic robot, hands-on mechanical or sensor adjustment, zero screen-bearing devices anywhere in frame, painterly cinematic illustrated rendering with visible crafted texture.

Follow these additional scene constraints: Keep the same screen-free physical robotics field-test semantics used in the previous discriminator. STYLE IS A HARD REQUIREMENT: use a premium painterly cinematic illustration with crafted brush-like texture, controlled stylization, rich atmospheric colour, and illustrated collectible-art language. Do not render this as a photograph, macro product photograph, DSLR image, stock photo, or photoreal commercial product shot.

Do not depict any of the following: generic coder at desk, glowing brain or meaningless holograms, readable code, logos, or brand names, monitor, laptop, tablet, phone, television, desktop computer, computer desk, workstation, display panel, screen glow, code, syntax highlighting, IDE, terminal, dashboard, waveform, editing interface, photograph, photorealistic rendering, macro product photography, stock photo, DSLR photo, product photography, hyperreal commercial photo, computer workstation.

Also avoid these global failure modes: text, logos, watermarks, card borders, rarity labels, UI elements, floating unrelated objects, duplicated key objects unless explicitly requested, flat procedural vector art, bland corporate illustration, generic stock-photo composition, muddy focal hierarchy, overabstract imagery, generic concept wallpaper, confusing mixtures of different hobbies, pseudo-text or gibberish lettering anywhere in the image, readable real-world brand names, logos, or trademarks, recognisable copyrighted film/game/cartoon characters or franchise costumes, collage, split-screen, comic-panel, or multi-panel layouts, photoreal stock-photo rendering unless explicitly requested by the hobby recipe, the hobby or interest name rendered anywhere in the image, title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, or body copy, poster, advertisement, magazine-cover, card-face, or editorial-page layout, text boxes, caption bands, lower-thirds, or deliberate blank space reserved for typography.

duplicated key objects unless explicitly requested
pseudo-text or gibberish lettering anywhere in the image

Use this activity-specific camera treatment: Low side three-quarter medium shot showing player, keyboard, mouse, headphones, and desktop tower together while excluding the entire display zone.

Keep these hobby-recognition cues visible: active play, engaged participant reaction, clear game or play-surface cue, generic desktop computer tower, full-size keyboard and mouse used actively, headphones plus focused seated gaming posture and reaction.

The scene must include: a visible PC Gaming play interaction, one generic unbranded desktop tower, active hands on keyboard and mouse, plain headphones, zero screen-bearing devices anywhere in frame.

Follow these additional scene constraints: This is a screenless PC-gaming recognition experiment. Do not add a monitor or substitute display. PC gaming must be recognizable only from the desktop tower, keyboard, mouse, headphones, seated player posture, hand positions, and focused reaction.
